editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News-category piece (531 words) using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. Neutral, descriptive tone throughout; no editorializing or sensationalism. No AI self-reference. Headline, summary, and Overview lead are all supported by the two independent sources (IAPP, SCMP); the state-affiliated outlets (Xinhua, Global Times) are used only for attributed supplementary details in later bullets, as the contributor bot described.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 source snapshots read from sources/2026-09/chinas-supreme-court-issues-nationwide-judicial-guidance-on-ai-disputes-setting-rules-on-deepfakes-and-liability/ (gunzip'd, sha256 verified against manifest.json — all 5 hashes match). (1) source-0.html.gz (IAPP, 'China sets a judicial benchmark for AI disputes'): full analysis piece read in full; confirms 24-provision opinion released 7 Sept 2026, ordinary-fault-liability default, the 'excessive liability ... discourage innovation' quote verbatim, evidentiary-burden shift for training data, and the two unresolved copyright questions verbatim ('significant disagreement over these issues during drafting'). Does NOT contain the word 'voice cloning' anywhere in the page (verified by case-insensitive grep — zero hits). (2) source-1.html.gz (SCMP): snapshot is a paywall-truncated preview (~1.7KB of extracted text, consistent with the page's own '3-MIN READ' teaser marker); confirms the 24-article opinion, the Civil Code/Cybersecurity Law/Copyright Law/PIPL list verbatim, and the exact quoted phrase 'everything from privacy breaches and sexual content to fraud and consumer protection' verbatim. Does mention 'voice cloning' explicitly ('rules on liability for deepfakes, voice cloning, hallucinations...'). The snapshot does NOT contain 'fault liability', 'excessive liability', or 'discourage innovation' anywhere (verified by grep — zero hits in all three cases) — the direct quote about avoiding excessive liability is therefore verified only against IAPP, not SCMP, despite the article co-citing both. (3) source-2.html.gz (Xinhua, english.news.cn): full wire piece read; confirms provider/user liability language, algorithmic price-discrimination liability, the injunction-for-irreversible-harm example, and the Zhou Jiahai quote verbatim ('We cannot expect every consumer to become an expert at spotting deception...'). (4) source-3.html.gz (globaltimes.cn/1370053.shtml): this page is explicitly byline 'By Xinhua' — it is the same Xinhua wire piece as source-2, republished on globaltimes.cn, not independent Global Times reporting. The Zhou Jiahai quote cited to 'Global Times' in the article is verbatim present on this page, so the citation is technically accurate to the URL used, but editorially it is a Xinhua wire story hosted on a Global Times page rather than original GT journalism — noted as a minor framing nuance, not a factual error. (5) source-4.html.gz (globaltimes.cn/1369996.shtml, byline 'By Global Times', citing Xinhua/People's Daily/CCTV as its own sources): confirms the deceased-individuals liability provision and the 'open for now, with clearer rules to be introduced when sufficient experience has been accumulated' phrase verbatim (the article's quote omits the source's trailing clause 'and conditions are in place', but everything inside the quotation marks is verbatim — acceptable truncation). No suspicious_patterns flagged in the manifest for any of the 5 sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Two source-attribution issues found, both confined to body 'What We Know' bullets (not the headline, summary, or Overview lead): (1) The bullet 'The guidance sets rules covering AI-generated deepfakes and voice cloning, ... according to IAPP' attributes 'voice cloning' to IAPP, but IAPP's snapshot never uses that term — 'voice cloning' appears only in SCMP, Xinhua, and Global Times. (2) The direct quote 'avoid imposing excessive liability while AI technology and the industry remain at an early stage of development, which could discourage innovation' is attributed to 'IAPP and the South China Morning Post' jointly, but the quote is verified verbatim only in the IAPP snapshot — it does not appear anywhere in the (paywall-truncated) SCMP snapshot. Both issues are minor over-attributions of true, verifiable claims to an extra source rather than fabrications; the underlying facts are accurate and each is independently confirmed by at least one of the two cited sources. Headline framing check requested by the human editor: verified independently — the headline ('...Setting Rules on Deepfakes and Liability'), the summary, and the entire Overview section rest exclusively on IAPP and SCMP citations; Xinhua and Global Times are used only in later, explicitly-attributed 'What We Know' bullets (Zhou Jiahai quote, algorithmic pricing, deceased-individuals provision, open-ended-issues quote) and never carry a headline/summary/lead claim alone. The framing discipline the contributor bot described was followed.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. Institutional actors (SPC, courts, businesses) are the subject of active-voice claims; no loaded language. The single direct quote from a state actor (Zhou Jiahai, SPC research office) is clearly attributed as a quote, not adopted as narration.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for 'Supreme People's Court' and related China-AI-judiciary coverage — no matches anywhere in the archive. This is a new topic, not previously covered.
concerns: 'AI-generated deepfakes and voice cloning' is attributed solely to IAPP in the body, but IAPP's snapshot never mentions voice cloning — the term is only substantiated by SCMP/Xinhua/Global Times.

The direct quote about avoiding 'excessive liability' and not discouraging innovation is co-attributed to SCMP, but is verified verbatim only in the IAPP snapshot; the SCMP snapshot (paywall-truncated) does not contain this quote.

The english.news.cn domain used for the Xinhua source is not on config/source_allowlist.txt (only xinhuanet.com is listed), which is why chief:review flagged a 'Sources not in allowlist' warning — this is a domain-string gap, not a credibility problem, since english.news.cn is Xinhua's own English-language portal.
recommendations: File a corrections record clarifying that 'voice cloning' is sourced to SCMP/Xinhua/Global Times, not IAPP, and that the 'excessive liability / discourage innovation' quote is sourced to IAPP alone.
Add english.news.cn to config/source_allowlist.txt as a recognized Xinhua domain alongside xinhuanet.com, to avoid future false-positive allowlist warnings on the same publisher.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, neutral, well-sourced News piece. Two minor over-attributions in supporting bullets (not the headline/summary/lead) are honestly correctable with a single corrections note; nothing rises to a REJECT-level fabrication or duplicate-coverage issue. The mixed-source framing discipline (independent sources for headline/summary/lead, explicitly-attributed state media only for supplementary bullet details) was verified and followed. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
